query: Reported superconducting high-entropy alloys are dominated by Nb-Ta matrices, while other studies concern titanium-rich systems based on heavy transition metals and partly ordered systems. Consequently, these precedents do not establish what controls superconductivity in high-entropy alloys outside the best-studied material classes. Within the defining constraint of a solid solution containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each, what governs superconducting behavior in such an uncharacterized high-entropy alloy, and why? State one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison against the starting material, predicted observations relative to the baseline, applicable boundary conditions, the earlier evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an outcome that would falsify it.

decision.trend: Research on high-entropy alloys has focused on their mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and superconductivity. Recent studies have explored the effects of different elements on the properties of these alloys, including the role of Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr in refractory high-entropy alloys. The discovery of superconductivity in a uranium-containing high-entropy alloy has also expanded the class of materials to include actinide elements.
decision.unsolved: The mechanism controlling superconductivity in high-entropy alloys outside the best-studied material classes remains unclear. The effects of different elements on the superconducting behavior of these alloys are not well understood, and the relationship between the alloy's composition and its superconducting properties is still unknown.
decision.why: A systematic variation of alloy composition would allow researchers to investigate the effects of different elements on the superconducting behavior of high-entropy alloys and identify the key factors controlling superconductivity in these materials.
